part: 10-way (2x5) 1.27mm shrouded box header, keyed, vertical, through-hole
description: Key chain connector - one at each end of each key board's IDC ribbon (CBL-CHAIN), on the main board and on the key board
package: THROUGH-HOLE vertical, 2x5, 1.27mm pitch - envelope config/body.yaml boards.chain_hdr_*
notes: Quantity is the tracked figure chain-connectors; do not restate it. PART: CNC Tech 3220-10-0100-00 [datasheets/connectors/CNCTECH-3220-XX-0100-00-1.27MM-BOX-HEADER-VERTICAL.pdf]. STOCKED: DigiKey 1175-1627-ND, status Active, six figures on the shelf on 2026-11-21 [web https://www.digikey.co.uk/en/products/detail/cnc-tech/3220-10-0100-00/3883661]. ANY KEYED, SHROUDED, VERTICAL 2x5 1.27mm BOX HEADER OF THIS PATTERN FITS THE BOARD - the size debug connectors use - but check its height and mouth depth against boards.chain_hdr_h and boards.chain_plug_proud first: the two mated sockets stand mouth to mouth (mechanical/drc.echo 'key-chain sockets clear of each other, mouth to mouth'). XKB X1270WV-2x05B-6TV01 (LCSC C2962225) is the candidate second source and is NOT cleared: its drawing could not be fetched (datasheets/MANIFEST.csv). Never fit an unshrouded or unkeyed 2x5 header: a socket can then go in reversed and put 3V3 on a ground pin. THROUGH-HOLE, so the cable's pull goes into the board, not into SMT pads. PINOUT, THE SAME AT BOTH ENDS OF BOTH RIBBONS (key-board-chain-pinmap): 1 GND, 2 SCK, 3 GND, 4 SH/LD, 5 GND, 6 SER, 7 GND, 8 QH, 9 GND, 10 3V3 - the odd row all ground, the even row the four signals and 3V3, and a ground between every signal in the ribbon (ADR 0001 item 1). Pin 6 is the key board's own serial input and pin 8 its own serial output, on both ribbons, so both key boards are wired alike. THE SAME PART AT EVERY J-CHAIN POSITION (chain-connectors): standing on the main board's top, and on each key board hanging from its underside mouth to mouth with the main board's, in the far band beside the LED row (mechanical/DESIGN.md; ADR 0028). Place the standard footprint on the key board's bottom side - do not hand-mirror it. The key board's header pin tails come up through the board toward the grounded key plate and stop short of it, with no window in the plate: mechanical/drc.echo 'J-CHAIN pin tails clear of the key plate' - seat the header flat. FITTED BY HAND WITH ITS KEY SLOT AT THE SILKSCREEN MARK: the 2x5 pad grid takes it turned 180 degrees too, and a header fitted backward takes its socket only with the ribbon twisted. The slot is in the wall over the odd row [datasheets/connectors/CNCTECH-3220-XX-0100-00-1.27MM-BOX-HEADER-VERTICAL.pdf]. Placed clear of the switches by mechanical/drc.echo 'chain headers on the left_hand boards clear of the switches' and its right_hand rule. Fitted with the switches (each board's fab/*-hand-assembly.csv)

part: 10-conductor 0.635mm flat ribbon with a 2x5 1.27mm IDC socket crimped at each end, straight
description: Key chain ribbon - one per key board, main board to key board, closed in one fold along the body
package: Made up to length - cut by mechanical/drc.echo 'key-chain ribbon to cut'
notes: One per key board (PCB-CLUSTER): the key chain's only conductors off the main board. MADE UP HERE, NOT BOUGHT ASSEMBLED: two IDC sockets, CNC Tech 3230-10-0103-00 [datasheets/connectors/CNCTECH-3230-XX-0103-00-1.27MM-IDC-SOCKET.pdf], crimped on 10 conductors of 0.635mm-pitch 30 AWG flat cable, the cable CBL-MCU-RIBBON is cut from [datasheets/connectors/3M-3754-FLAT-CABLE-0.025IN-30AWG-PVC.pdf]. A STRAIGHT CABLE: BOTH SOCKETS ON THE SAME FACE OF THE RIBBON, THEIR KEYS FACING THE SAME WAY ALONG IT, pin 1 on the same edge conductor - so conductor n is J-CHAIN pin n at both ends (key-board-chain-pinmap). Laid flat, one socket's key then faces its own ribbon and the other's faces away from it; folded closed, each meets its header's slot (key-chain-loom.md, Pin numbering), and the ends are not interchangeable without a twist. LENGTH: cut the ribbon to mechanical/drc.echo 'key-chain ribbon to cut', a socket flush at each end; the free length that leaves is 'key-chain ribbon length (derived)'. It lets the key plate be held raised off its columns, with both key boards on it, while the main board's sockets are plugged (config/body.yaml routing.chain_service, routing.chain_raise; ADR 0025). CLOSED: the ribbon leaves both sockets flat, the same way along the body, and its spare length makes ONE fold - no turn at either socket - so it never stands across the LED row's light (ADR 0028) (drc.echo 'key-chain ribbon closed: hairpin leg and fold radius', 'key-chain ribbon fold no tighter than its bend radius', 'key-chain ribbon hairpin clear of the columns'); which way each folds is routing.chain_fold. Width and thickness: routing.chain_ribbon_w and routing.chain_ribbon_t. TO TAKE THE KEY PLATE OFF: undo its column screws, raise it, unplug the main board's sockets, pulling each straight up by its body, not by the ribbon. METER EVERY CABLE BEFORE IT IS FIRST POWERED, spares and replacements included: conductor 10 reaches the far socket's position 10 and conductor 2 its position 2, and no two neighbours are shorted (hardware/boards/key-board-lh/README.md, Bring-up). OPEN, M4: boards.chain_plug_proud and boards.chain_plug_cable, taken from the two drawings and measured on the first mated pair, set the room between the two sockets and the fold's radius

description: Series damping at the chain driving end on SCK, SH/LD and the chain-end SER
notes: On the main board where the MCU's pins arrive, before anything else on the net. SCK and SH/LD each reach four registers (U-KEYS): right_thumb and left_thumb on the main board, and one at the far end of each key board's ribbon, over up to the main board's length (mechanical/drc.echo 'main board (derived)'). At that length an MCU edge sees a line rather than a lump [calc, key-chain-loom.md]. Edge-rate damping at the source - NOT series termination, which ADR 0001 rejected (as R-TERM-CHAIN) for a line that drops on four registers. Same 100R as R-SPI-SER. FIT IT. SIMULATED (hardware/interfaces/key-chain-loom/sim): with it, SCK reaches the left-hand key board's register with no swing back through the register's hysteresis and no overshoot past its clamp at every corner of drive strength, edge rate and load ('sck-to-key-board'); without it, at the strong-drive, fast-edge, light-load corner, SCK swings back through the hysteresis (a double clock) and past the clamp both ways ('sck-without-series-resistor'). The GPIO's output impedance and edge are estimates (Espressif publishes neither, nor IBIS), so E14 still scopes SCK at that register. 1206, 1/4 W: a sustained output fault puts 33 mA through it, 109 mW, which is 87 % of an 0805's 1/8 W and 44 % of this [calc; ds UNIROYAL-THICK-FILM-CHIP-RESISTOR-0805W8F.pdf, 1206 = 1/4 W, 200 V]. UNI-ROYAL 1206W4F1000T5E, LCSC C17901

description: Series resistor at left_thumb's QH on HOP_LT_RH, the hop to right_hand
notes: Owner, 2026-10-01 (pre-layout review A5-2). On the MAIN BOARD at left_thumb's QH, before the hop leaves for the right_hand ribbon's conductor 6. right_hand is clocked through the same ribbon, later than left_thumb; without this resistor the hop's data could reach right_hand's SER before its clock and held only on a CLK-to-QH delay TI does not publish. With 2.2k the RC with the ribbon and right_hand's input holds the data past right_hand's clock at every corner with ZERO propagation delay, and it still arrives well inside the 1us period (key-chain-loom/sim hop-hold-lt-to-rh; key-chain-loom.md, The hop hold time). 0603WAF2201T5E, LCSC C4190, JLC basic

description: ESD protection on the MCU pins the key chain brings to the main board's ribbon headers
notes: FIT BOTH (ADR 0018; the second, owner 2026-10-03, D2: 'Yes, all 4 channels'). AT THE left_hand J-CHAIN (J4): SCK, SH/LD and the chain-end SER (IO38, IO7, IO33, each on the connector side of its R-CHAIN-SER); the fourth is spare. AT THE right_hand J-CHAIN (J5): SCK, SH/LD, HOP_LT_RH and HOP_RH_RT - J5 exposes the same two MCU pins as J4, and one array at J4 is a board's length from them. The chain's QH into the MCU (IO40) comes from right_thumb on the main board and reaches no connector. Return to PWR_GND, the main board's ground pour, with a via at pin 2. WHY: with the lid off and a socket unplugged, a main-board J-CHAIN header exposes MCU pins behind 100R to a hand - and the sockets are plugged in every time the lid goes back on. It cannot be added once the board is made. The second array's 30 pF on HOP_LT_RH, behind R-HOP-SER, is in key-chain-loom/sim's hold deck. PACKAGE: SP0504BAHTG is SOT23-5 with 4 CH per the banked SP0504BAHT.pdf p.1 ordering table; SOT23-6 is SP0505BAHTG with 5 CH. All channels share one common pin. These and U-TVS-SPI are separate packages because each clamps at its own connector

part: Ferrite bead 600R @ 100MHz or more, DCR 0.1R or less, rated 0.5A or more
description: Series isolation on the 3V3 conductor of each key board's ribbon, on the main board
notes: ONE PER RIBBON, in series between the main board's 3V3 (DEV_3V3 - the Matrix's ME6217C33M5G LDO, reaching the main board on CBL-MCU-RIBBON) and that ribbon's conductor 10 (main-board J-CHAIN pin 10). right_thumb, left_thumb and R-SER-TERM stay on DEV_3V3 directly. IT IS ISOLATION, NOT PROTECTION: it keeps a key board's register edges off the rail that is also the MCP3202's reference. SHORT-CIRCUIT PROTECTION IS THE LDO'S OWN (ADR 0018): datasheets/discrete-and-power/ME6217C33M5G.pdf p.1 'a built-in overcurrent protector' and thermal shutdown at 160C; p.4 Ishort 350mA TYPICAL at VOUT = 0V, with no min or max. The short to expect is a socket forced or a ribbon pinched across conductors 9/10 (main-board J-CHAIN pins 9/10) at reassembly: the whole 3V3 rail collapses, the Matrix does not start, and it is seen on the bench before the lid is closed. VERIFY AT E1: short one ribbon's 3V3 to GND through 1 ohm at J-CHAIN, confirm the rail limits and the Matrix restarts when it is removed. RATINGS: rated current at or above 0.5A, because the bead carries the LDO's limit (350mA typ) for as long as a short lasts [calc]. DCR 0.1R or less: at the chain's whole key-scan-current (every key closed) that is under 3mV [calc]. THE PART: Murata BLM21SP601SN1D - 600R +/-25% at 100MHz, DCR 0.060R max, 1.5A at 125C [datasheets/discrete-and-power/MURATA-BLM21-SN1-REFERENCE-SPEC-JENF243A-0005.pdf], the one candidate with margin on both DCR and current; JLC C3716677 (Extended: JLC's Basic GZ2012D601TF fails DCR at 0.30R). Second source TDK MPZ2012S601AT000 (0.100R max, at the limit). SIMULATED (hardware/interfaces/key-chain-loom/sim, Murata's own model of this part, banked): below its resistive band it is several microhenries, not the ~1uH once assumed, and with the key board's C-DECOUPLE-165 it forms a lightly damped LC whose frequency and peak are in sim/results.yaml (rail-impedance-*); the key board's rail stays inside its limit with C-BULK-CHAIN NOT fitted (sim 'rail-as-ordered'), and the key board's clocking moves DEV_3V3 by under one MCP3202 LSB. Murata states the model for 1MHz-3GHz, so at the LC's frequency it is extrapolated: bring-up step 6 confirms on the real rail

description: The rail's reservoir, one on each key board's 3V3, beside J-CHAIN's 3V3 pin
notes: ONE PER KEY BOARD, on its root sheet (C7 on the left-hand board, C8 on the right), machine-placed; the sheet names the part bought. FB-CHAIN and C-DECOUPLE-165 form a lightly damped LC (FB-CHAIN row), and this part's ESR damps it. The simulation (hardware/interfaces/key-chain-loom/sim) holds the rail inside its limit with it fitted ('rail-as-ordered') and without it ('rail-without-bulk'), so a board built without it still works: it is fitted because it costs cents and makes the rail quieter, not because the rail needs it.

description: Pull-up on the chain-end serial input, on the main board
notes: left_hand's SER, which leaves on conductor 6 of its ribbon (main-board J-CHAIN pin 6, key-board pin 7). ON THE MAIN BOARD at that ribbon's J-CHAIN, on the connector side of R-CHAIN-SER - so the two key boards stay identical. Holds the chain-end input high when nothing drives it, which is the tied-off case ADR 0001 specified. If firmware DRIVES it from IO33, the 100R series wins against 10k to within 33mV of the rail (3.3V x 100/10100) - so an end-to-end self-test (shift a known pattern through all 32 bits, and through both ribbons in both directions) is a FIRMWARE choice rather than a board choice. Fitted. Whether firmware uses it is a firmware choice, made at E4
